dedupe_keys.name: divi intensive care register daily icu capacity and covid 19 icu occupancy in germany by state and district rki open data

description: This Robert Koch Institute dataset publishes daily intensive care capacity and COVID-19 intensive care occupancy in Germany, taken from the DIVI-Intensivregister, the digital platform to which every German hospital with intensive care beds must report by noon each day. The RKI prepares and releases it on GitHub and Zenodo. Coverage: Germany since the COVID-19 pandemic; the register started collecting data on 17 March 2020 from the ARDS network's reporting portal and went live as a new platform on 3-4 April 2020; files give national figures for adults and children (split into neonatal and paediatric units), state-level figures for adults, district-level COVID-19 and capacity series from 24 April 2020 to 15 September 2025, age groups of COVID-19 ICU cases, care levels and ventilation types for fixed periods; variables include the number of reporting ICU areas, occupied and free beds and COVID-19 cases. Format and access: CSV files with variable documentation in German, updated daily at national and state level, on GitHub with a Zenodo DOI (10.5281/zenodo.23015647); free. Licence: CC-BY-4.0 (LICENSE file). Caveats: data are aggregated, not per hospital; district-level and some breakdowns stopped in 2025 or 2023; documentation is in German. Simulation uses: hospital surge capacity baselines for emergency response and capacity planning of health services during epidemics and disasters. Related records: the German hospital directory (data-verzeichnis-der-krankenhauser-und-vorsorge-oder-rehabilitationseinrichtungen-p02616) lists the facilities, and RKI emergency department surveillance (data-rki-emergency-department-surveillance) is a companion RKI dataset.
